stories.title: What to do when you find an injured street dog
stories.excerpt: A calm, safe first response can make all the difference.
stories.body: First, pause and look for immediate danger. Keep traffic and crowds at a safe distance. An injured animal may be frightened, so avoid sudden movements and do not attempt to lift them unless there is immediate danger. Offer water only if the animal is alert and able to swallow. Note the exact location, take a clear photo from a safe distance and contact a local animal rescue group or veterinarian. If safe, stay nearby until help arrives. Never give human painkillers. Small, steady actions can save a life.

stories.title: Why sterilization is the kindest way to manage strays
stories.excerpt: A humane, long-term approach rooted in health and coexistence.
stories.body: Humane animal birth control, paired with anti-rabies vaccination and post-operative care, helps reduce future suffering. It must be carried out by trained veterinary teams under applicable local rules. Community participation matters: identify animals, support safe transport, and help monitor recovery. Sterilization is not a quick fix, but a sustained programme can improve animal welfare and neighbourhood health.

stories.title: Animal protection laws every Indian should know
stories.excerpt: A friendly starting point for understanding our shared responsibilities.
stories.body: India has several laws and rules that address animal welfare, including the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and rules governing animal birth control. Local procedures and legal remedies can vary, so document incidents safely and seek guidance from the appropriate authorities or a qualified legal professional. Do not confront an alleged offender if it puts you or an animal at risk. Compassion works best when paired with careful, lawful action.

stories.title: How to feed street animals responsibly
stories.excerpt: Kindness is wonderful. A little planning makes it safer, too.
stories.body: Choose a consistent, safe spot away from traffic, building entrances and school gates. Keep feeding areas clean and remove leftovers. Offer species-appropriate food and fresh water; avoid spicy, salty or cooked bones. Coordinate with neighbours and local feeders, and support vaccination and sterilization efforts. Feeding should never block access or create a hazard. Respectful routines help animals and communities coexist.

stories.title: Summer heat care for pets and strays
stories.excerpt: Shade, water and knowing when to call for help.
stories.body: Heat can become dangerous quickly. Provide clean water and access to shade. Avoid walking dogs on hot pavement during peak sun, and never leave an animal inside a parked vehicle. Watch for heavy panting, weakness, vomiting or collapse; these are urgent warning signs. Move the animal to a cooler place and contact a veterinarian immediately. Do not use ice-cold baths unless a vet advises it.

stories.title: Why adopt, not shop
stories.excerpt: A home changes two lives: theirs, and yours.
stories.body: Adoption gives an animal a chance to belong and makes room for another animal who needs help. Meet the animal, ask about their health and behaviour, and choose a match that fits your home and routine. Give them time to settle in. Responsible adoption is a commitment to food, healthcare, safety and patience for their whole life. Home is a verb.
